heroCommands.comment: Open your AI CLI in it

sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: career-ops is an open-source AI job search agent that runs inside the AI coding CLI you already use, such as Claude Code or Codex. Paste a job and it checks the posting is live, scores it against your CV, tailors your CV and drafts your answers. You press Submit.
sixtySeconds.problem: Job seekers send many applications into silence. career-ops helps you apply to fewer, better-fitting roles by evaluating each posting against your experience and telling you when not to apply.
whoFor: Job seekers comfortable with a terminal
Users of Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Qwen and similar CLIs
People applying to tech roles at many companies
Anyone who wants application data kept on their own machine
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for a local, human-in-the-loop job search assistant that never submits or emails for you. It needs an AI CLI and a model, which may cost money.
requirements: An AI coding CLI such as Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Qwen, agy or Grok
Optional: Playwright Chromium for PDF generation

overview: career-ops is a set of modes and scripts that your AI CLI runs. On first launch it asks for your CV, profile and target roles by chat, with nothing to configure by hand. After that you paste a job URL or description and it runs a full pipeline: a liveness check, an A to H evaluation, a report, a tailored ATS-friendly CV PDF and a tracker row.

Other modes scan 180+ preconfigured company job boards on Ashby, Greenhouse, Lever and Wellfound, draft cover letters and emails, find a contact and draft a note, prepare interviews, analyse rejection patterns and help with offers and negotiation. A terminal dashboard shows your pipeline.

The README is explicit about what it will not do: it never auto-submits an application, never sends an email, has no telemetry or backend, and advises against applying below a 4.0/5 score. A code check stops CV PDFs with facts not found in your CV, but you should still read every CV before sending it.

troubleshooting.solution: Install Chromium's system libraries with your distro's package manager; Playwright's docs list them.

troubleshooting.solution: Ask in plain language, for example Run the career-ops scan mode.
Give it more about your CV and preferences; the README says first runs are rough.
